dedupe_keys.name: minecan canada wide benchmark dataset for mining detection from satellite imagery memorial university

description: A benchmark of 1,519 hand-annotated image patches of mining sites across Canada, each 750 by 750 pixels of high-resolution RGB imagery, with pixel-level segmentation masks and object detection bounding boxes. The Zenodo record says the images were captured manually from Google Earth between 14 January and 7 February 2025, and that mine locations were found with the FINEPRINT viewer, used only as a geographic reference. Published on 16 February 2026 by Manjula Ariyarathne, Thumeera R. Wanasinghe and Weimin Huang, it is one zip file (MineCan) of about 4.3 GB, free to download under CC BY 4.0; a later version exists. Coverage is Canada. Caveats: images come from Google Earth, whose own terms may limit reuse, the capture dates of the underlying imagery vary, and the site sample follows FINEPRINT mapped mines. For simulation it gives training data for models that map mine footprints across Canada, to keep exposure layers of mining operations near rivers, roads and communities up to date. Related catalogue records include the Maus global mining polygons, the global ML-ready mining area dataset and EuroMineNet.
